title: Android 17 is the first since 3.x to add new APIs without releasing to the AOSP
why_read: A concrete governance change in how Android exposes new APIs is genuinely relevant to Android developers tracking platform openness trends.
analysis: The claim is that Android 17 introduces new public APIs without first landing the corresponding code in the open-source AOSP repository, a shift from past practice. This matters because AOSP visibility affects custom ROM developers, security researchers, and companies building Android forks who rely on inspecting implementation code. If accurate, it signals a further tightening of Google's control over the platform's genuinely open portions, which has real downstream effects for the broader Android ecosystem.
